Technical Analysis using R — Preliminary Stage

BDA400 Data Science Tools and Techniques · Assignment 2

Viktoriia Agafonova

November 18, 2026

AI Assistance Declaration: I used Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude desktop app, 2026-11-18) for drafting the structure of the functions, this R Markdown layout and comments. I verified outputs by running and knitting the code in RStudio and checking the tables against the downloaded data. All final calculations are done by R. I am responsible for the accuracy and originality of this work.

1 Project configuration

The portfolio is defined in portfolio.txt — one ticker symbol per line.

portfolio_file <- "portfolio.txt"
cat(readLines(portfolio_file), sep = "\n")
## AAPL
## MSFT
## GOOGL
## AMZN
## NVDA
symbols <- read_portfolio(portfolio_file)
symbols
## [1] "AAPL"  "MSFT"  "GOOGL" "AMZN"  "NVDA"

Analysis period (daily data from Yahoo Finance via quantmod):

start_date <- as.Date("2025-11-01")
end_date   <- as.Date("2026-11-01")   # 'to' is exclusive in getSymbols()
ma_windows <- c(20, 50)               # moving-average windows (trading days)

2 Importing stock data

load_stock_data() reads portfolio.txt, downloads the data for every symbol with quantmod::getSymbols() and returns one data frame per symbol (columns: Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, Adjusted). With assign_to_env = TRUE it also creates a separate data frame named after each symbol (e.g. AAPL).

stocks <- load_stock_data(portfolio_file, from = start_date, to = end_date,
                          assign_to_env = TRUE)
vapply(stocks, nrow, integer(1))   # trading days loaded per symbol
##  AAPL  MSFT GOOGL  AMZN  NVDA 
##   250   250   250   250   250
str(stocks[[1]])
## 'data.frame':    250 obs. of  7 variables:
##  $ Date    : Date, format: "2025-11-03" "2025-11-04" ...
##  $ Open    : num  270 268 269 268 270 ...
##  $ High    : num  271 271 272 273 272 ...
##  $ Low     : num  266 268 267 268 267 ...
##  $ Close   : num  269 270 270 270 268 ...
##  $ Volume  : num  50194600 49274800 43683100 51204000 48227400 ...
##  $ Adjusted: num  268 269 269 269 267 ...

3 Computing statistics

calculate_statistics() takes one stock’s data frame and computes, on the Close price:

  • Mean, median, standard deviation (base R);
  • Mode — prices are continuous, so they are rounded to whole dollars before counting the most frequent value (get_mode());
  • Simple moving averages of 20 and 50 days (TTR::SMA());
  • extra context: min, max, last close, mean daily return and daily volatility.

Results are stored in a structured list: a one-row summary data frame and a moving_averages data frame for each stock. calculate_all_statistics() applies it to the whole portfolio.

results <- calculate_all_statistics(stocks, price_col = "Close", ma_windows = ma_windows)
str(results$by_symbol[[1]], max.level = 1)
## List of 2
##  $ summary        :'data.frame': 1 obs. of  14 variables:
##  $ moving_averages:'data.frame': 250 obs. of  4 variables:

3.1 Portfolio summary

kable(results$summary_table[, c("Symbol", "Observations", "Mean", "Median", "Mode",
                                "Std_Dev", "Min", "Max", "Last_Close",
                                "Last_SMA_20", "Last_SMA_50")],
      digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Symbol", "Days", "Mean", "Median", "Mode", "Std. dev.",
                    "Min", "Max", "Last close", "SMA 20", "SMA 50"),
      caption = "Table 1. Close-price statistics by stock (USD)")

4.2 Portfolio overview

plot_portfolio_growth(stocks)

Figure 1. Growth of $100 invested at the start of the period

4.3 Stock-by-stock

for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  df    <- stocks[[sym]]
  stats <- results$by_symbol[[sym]]

  cat("\n\n### ", sym, "\n\n", sep = "")

  cat("**Quote summary**\n\n")
  print(kable(build_quote_summary(df), col.names = c("", "")))

  cat("\n\n**Latest 5 trading days**\n\n")
  print(kable(tail(df, 5), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
              format.args = list(big.mark = ",")))

  cat("\n\n**Statistics (Close price)**\n\n")
  print(kable(statistics_table(stats)))

  cat("\n\n")
  plot_stock_chart(df, sym)
  cat("\n\n")
  print(plot_price_with_ma(stats, sym))
  cat("\n\n")
}
